C1 tests/core/task-state.test.ts.reason: Every emptiness assertion in this file is pinned by a non-empty counterpart on the SAME value: `changed` is asserted `[]` on a re-statement and `['blocked']` / `['next']` on real changes; `taskStateLines` is asserted `[]` on an empty state and `['Goal','Next','Blocked','Just finished']` on a populated one. The detector looks for `toBeGreaterThan` / `.has(` / `length).toBe(N)` and does not recognise `toEqual(['x'])` as a size pin. Adding one of those shapes here would satisfy the regex without testing anything new.

C1 tests/core/task-state-store.test.ts.reason: Same shape as the sibling file: `changed` is asserted `[]` for a no-op write and `['blocked']` when a clear actually happens, and `expect(row).toBeUndefined()` for the no-op is pinned by four other tests that read the row back and assert its tag, title and observations. Not vacuous; the pin is just not in a shape the regex matches.

C1 tests/cli/upgrade-plugin.test.ts.reason: the `.toBe(0)` occurrences assert child-process EXIT CODES (success), not empty collections; the file also asserts non-empty stderr/stdout content on every failure path and pins a semver comparison (4.10.0 beats 4.9.0), so nothing is vacuously empty. The detector's regex cannot tell an exit-code zero from an empty-set zero.
